'''Cyntha Anne Struthers''' (born 1953 or 1954){{r|born}} is a Canadian mathematical statistician whose research topics include [[missing data]] in [[longitudinal study|longitudinal studies]] and [[proportional hazards model]]s. She is an associate professor of statistics and [[actuarial science]] at the [[University of Waterloo]],{{r|waterloo}} and the former president of the [[Caucus for Women in Statistics]].{{r|cwstat}}

==Education and career==
After earning a bachelor's degree in mathematics,{{r|waterloo}} and a master's degree in statistics in 1977 from the University of Waterloo, Struthers took a teaching position in mathematics at the university before gaining the confidence to return to doctoral study.{{r|sju}} She completed her Ph.D. in statistics at Waterloo in 1985); her doctoral dissertation, ''Asymptotic properties of linear rank tests with censored data'', was supervised by Jack Kalbfleisch.{{r|mg}}

She began working as a mathematics professor at [[St. Jerome's University]] in 1985,{{r|sju}} and chaired the department there,{{r|ppf}} before moving to the University of Waterloo in 2014 when the mathematics programs at St. Jerome's were consolidated into the University of Waterloo.{{r|subtract}}

==Service==
Struthers was the founding chair of the Canadian section of the [[Caucus for Women in Statistics]], from 1987 to 1989,{{r|ppf}} and served as president of the Caucus for Women in Statistics for the 1991 term.{{r|cwstat}} She 
chaired the Committee on Women in Statistics of the [[Statistical Society of Canada]] from 1998 to 2000.{{r|ppf}}
